description: Opt-in aggressive unsigned-DLL drive sweep monitor. Mirrors the PS script's Invoke-UnsignedDLLRemover: walks ready Fixed/Removable/Network drive roots (plus an explicit C:\Windows\System32 pass) for *.dll/*.winmd capped at 500 per drive, verifies Authenticode, and quarantines validly-unsigned candidates through Sentinel's EXISTING QuarantineManager (delete-on-reboot handles locked files; no process-kill shelling-out). Entire monitor gated behind a new compiled config flag EnableAggressiveUnsignedDllSweep defaulting FALSE. Modeled on LnkUncGuard, added to the EXISTING PsPortedMonitors.cs, registered in the Service's SystemIntegrity MonitorGroup only (NOT the Critical group, NOT the Agent - LnkUncGuard is not registered in the Agent). Independent of FEAT-002 except both edit src/Sentinel.Service/Program.cs; sequence FEAT-001 first to minimize Program.cs merge friction.
steps: Read context.json and this file FIRST; it replaces re-exploration. Then study LnkUncGuard in src/Sentinel.Core/Monitors/PsPortedMonitors.cs and the QuarantineManager/SecurityValidation/ModuleIdentity signatures named in context.json.

In src/Sentinel.Core/Models.cs add 'public bool EnableAggressiveUnsignedDllSweep { get; set; } = false;' to SentinelConfig next to EnableHardwarePmuMonitor / EnableDynamicSandboxing (the 'Optional modern detection extensions' block ~line 228-233), with a one-line doc comment that it is a deliberate opt-in aggressive non-default mode (compiled default FALSE; disk JSON does not enable it). Default MUST be false.

In src/Sentinel.Core/Monitors/PsPortedMonitors.cs (do NOT create a new file) add 'public sealed class AggressiveUnsignedDllSweepMonitor : BackgroundService' modeled on LnkUncGuard. Ctor-inject DetectionEngine, QuarantineManager, ILogger<AggressiveUnsignedDllSweepMonitor>, and SentinelConfig (DI-registered via AddSingleton(config); do not 'new' it). Instance ConcurrentDictionary<string,DateTime> alert-cooldown (OrdinalIgnoreCase) and ConcurrentDictionary<string,byte> quarantined-hash cache (no static mutable state).

ExecuteAsync: if !_config.EnableAggressiveUnsignedDllSweep, log '[AggressiveUnsignedDllSweep] disabled' and return immediately. Otherwise log start, await Task.Delay(settle, ct) (catch OperationCanceledException -> return), then while(!ct.IsCancellationRequested) call ScanAllAsync(ct) with periodic Task.Delay(ScanInterval, ct) - same loop shape and same catch/log discipline as LnkUncGuard (every catch logs at Debug minimum). Thread ct through all async methods.

Add internal async Task<int> ScanAllAsync(CancellationToken ct = default): enumerate drive roots via System.IO.DriveInfo.GetDrives() filtered to DriveType.Fixed|Removable|Network and d.IsReady, plus an explicit C:\Windows\System32 pass (parity with the script; those files get skipped by ShouldSkipPath). For each root enumerate *.dll and *.winmd, Take(500) per drive, and for each file call the evaluate/quarantine helper. Catch and log per-file errors; respect ct.

Add internal static bool ShouldSkipPath(string path): return true (skip) when SecurityValidation.IsOsCriticalPath(path) || ModuleIdentity.IsOsServicingPath(path) || ModuleIdentity.IsKeepTree(path) || the lowercased full path contains any of: \windows\system32\, \windows\syswow64\, \windows\winsxs\, \windows\servicing\, \program files\, \program files (x86)\, \assembly\ (GAC), the Sentinel install dir, the quarantine dir, or '\'+HoneypotDllMonitor.HoneypotSubdir+'\'. Compute on Path.GetFullPath(path).ToLowerInvariant() inside try/catch; on error return true (fail closed - do not quarantine).

Evaluate/quarantine helper: skip if ShouldSkipPath(path). If SecurityValidation.VerifyAuthenticodeSignature(path) is true -> skip. Else (unsigned candidate) honor alert-cooldown unless the file hash is in the quarantined cache (re-quarantine re-dropped files). Call await _quarantine.QuarantineFileAtomicAsync(path, forceQuarantineSigned: true) (do NOT reimplement quarantine; the manager still refuses IsOsCriticalPath internally - rely on that safety net). On a non-null result, record the hash in the cache and emit via _detectionEngine.EmitAsync a DetectionEvent (RuleName e.g. 'DLL Sweep: Unsigned Module Quarantined', Tier=DetectionTier.Tier1Behavioral, AuthorizedResponse=ResponseAction.Quarantine, Confidence ~0.85, ProcessName='dllsweep', ProcessId=0, SignalType=SignalType.SuspiciousProcess, Evidence/Reasoning naming path+signature status+quarantine result, Metadata with Path/SignatureStatus/Quarantined/QuarantinePath) - mirror LnkUncGuard's emission.

DO NOT route process-kill through DllUnloadEngine: its OnSideloadDllDroppedAsync only acts on hijack-NAME plants/COM payloads, not arbitrary unsigned DLLs (verified in exploration). Quarantine-with-delete-on-reboot alone is the approved fallback; never shell out to taskkill.

Register in src/Sentinel.Service/Program.cs ONLY: add services.AddSingleton<AggressiveUnsignedDllSweepMonitor>(); next to the other SystemIntegrity singletons (block ~line 795 starting with StateReconciliationMonitor), AND add the tuple ("AggressiveUnsignedDllSweepMonitor", s => s.GetRequiredService<AggressiveUnsignedDllSweepMonitor>()) to the SafeMonitorResolver.Build(sp, ...) list inside the 'Group 5: System Integrity' AddSingleton<IHostedService> factory (the list ending with StateReconciliationMonitor). Do NOT add to the Critical group. Do NOT register in the Agent.

Add tests/Sentinel.Tests/AggressiveUnsignedDllSweepMonitorTests.cs (xUnit). Primary tests target the pure static AggressiveUnsignedDllSweepMonitor.ShouldSkipPath(string): assert true for C:\Windows\System32\kernel32.dll, C:\Windows\SysWOW64\x.dll, C:\Windows\WinSxS\x.dll, C:\Program Files\app\x.dll (refuses OS-critical/system paths); assert false for C:\Users\x\Downloads\evil.dll (would be a candidate). Keep it filesystem-light and elevation-free; ShouldSkipPath is pure so no temp files needed.
Build and run tests; fix any compile/test errors introduced by this feature.

Set this FEAT's status to 'completed' and record in findings anything FEAT-002 or the merge step needs (e.g. exact Program.cs edit locations touched). Commit locally on the branch; never push. Do not bump version.txt.

Monitor is registered in the Service SystemIntegrity MonitorGroup (singleton + resolver tuple) and NOT in the Critical group and NOT in the Agent.
Running dotnet test passes new ShouldSkipPath tests proving OS-critical/system paths are skipped and a user-writable drop is not.
dotnet build -c Debug compiles with no errors.
